_v1_notes.THREAT ITEM|SCREENING POINT: a firearm in cabin baggage is N for hold explosive detection, which never sees cabin items. A hold IED is N for the walk-through detector and N for cabin X-ray. Liquids are N for the walk-through and N for hold detection. A blade on the body is N for both baggage screening points.
_v1_notes.THREAT ITEM|CONCEALMENT: a firearm carried on the body is N here - that is the blade case. A hold IED on the body is N by definition of hold baggage. Liquids cannot be disassembled, cannot be hidden in electronics usefully, and are N on the body at volume. A blade is N openly in a bag and N inside electronics.
_v1_notes.SCREENING POINT|CONCEALMENT: the walk-through detector sees only body-carried items, so open-in-bag, disassembled and in-electronics are all N. Cabin X-ray and hold detection are both N for body-carried. Behavioural observation detects no object at all, so every concealment is N.
_v1_notes.SCREENING POINT|PASSENGER TYPE: airport staff bypass passenger screening entirely, so the walk-through, cabin X-ray and hold detection are all N; only behavioural observation applies. A transit passenger not re-screened is N for the walk-through and cabin X-ray at this airport, though hold baggage may still be screened on transfer.
_v1_notes.SCREENING POINT|OUTCOME: every screening point is N for detected-after-boarding - by then screening is complete and the point played no part.
_v1_notes.CONCEALMENT|OUTCOME: every concealment method is N for no-item-present, which by definition involves no concealment.
